target_customer: UK nightlife and urban-culture event organisers/promoters (1,027 signed up by March 2014) who pay a ticket commission; clubgoers as buyers
problem: Promoters of short-lead-time urban music nights lacked a ticketing platform fitted to them; Eventbrite skewed corporate and Ticketmaster did not suit nightlife.
business_model: Ticketing marketplace, 10% commission or 1 GBP minimum per ticket (2014)

founders.name: Louise Broni-Mensah
founders.background_notes: Managed a hip-hop artist and promoted events on the side; solo, non-technical, first-time founder (YC blog).

competitors.name: Eventbrite
competitors.what: Self-service ticketing; used by some promoters moving online

competitors.name: Ticketmaster
competitors.what: Incumbent ticketing, seen by founder as poorly suited to short-notice nightlife

competitors.name: YPlan
competitors.what: London app for last-minute event discovery and booking

technical_complexity.rationale: Ticketing marketplace and organiser tools; payments and mobile apps but standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Two-sided marketplace with niche organiser relationships and community focus, but ticketing was a crowded, copyable category.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of incumbents copying or buying Shoobs; it remains independent and in 2024 partnered with Songkick (Warner) for event listings.

market_need_then: Per TechCrunch (2014-03): 1,027 organisers signed up and over 100,000 tickets sold in 2013 in the UK.

branding.name_origin: Slang for a party (TechCrunch 2014 via Urban Dictionary; Wikipedia)

identity.voice_and_tone: Urban-culture, event-focused positioning for Black music and culture (MBW/Music Week partnership coverage)

branding.brand_signature: Positioning as a ticketing and marketing partner for Black-culture events and festivals (e.g. Afro Nation) per trade press snippets
branding.community_and_virality: Partnership press (Songkick 2024) and festival ticketing roles show brand recognition in its niche

brand_strength.rationale: Niche-community brand with trade-press coverage and a Songkick partnership; no evidence of mascot, merch or viral brand effect.

outcome_analysis: Shoobs found a niche in UK urban-culture event ticketing with a founder close to the scene, selling 100,000+ tickets in 2013, and survives a decade later with festival clients and a 2024 Songkick partnership. No verified funding beyond YC's small cheque is public, so it looks like a slow-growth niche business rather than a venture-scale breakout.
notes: TechCrunch (2014-03) reports just under $100,000 raised from YC and YC Ventures; exact figure and date not stated so no round recorded. Aggregator totals ($120K, $330K, $521K) conflict and are unverified. Founding year conflicts: YC says 2013, Wikipedia says started 2010, a database says 2009. Wikipedia lists earlier grants (Bright Ideas Trust, Shell LiveWIRE 2010) without amounts. No outcome events found; latest news May 2024 names her CEO. Competitor list taken from the 2014 TechCrunch article only. Directory status Active. Completeness pass: Round recorded from TechCrunch (March 2014): just under $100,000 from YC and YC Ventures, exact amount and date not stated so both null. CB Insights reports $330K over 3 rounds (EchoVC, Morgan Stanley Inclusive Ventures Lab, YC) which is larger than the recorded round; the gap is not itemised.
